A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same probabilistic model of neural responses to videos. All 18 pages of v2 and 31 pages of v3, including appendices, figures, tables, equations, and the later checklist, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original SENSORIUM experiments, including predictive correlations, likelihoods, latent-variable analyses, OOD evaluation, and extrapolation to held-out neurons.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds experiments involving alternative losses, response distributions, transformer cores, behavioral inputs, and CEBRA.

M1.justification: The principal ZIG model, Gaussian latent state, GRU encoder, and conditional inference procedure remain unchanged. Appendices G-I add tested adaptations using Poisson-loss training, Gaussian and flow-based response distributions, and a Vision Transformer core.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ten SENSORIUM mice and retain naturalistic-video prediction, OOD stimuli, behavioral analyses, and held-out-neuron extrapolation. The mouse-number swaps match the same recording IDs in v2 Table 11 and v3 Table 12; the added model comparisons do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 substantially broadens the evaluated comparators: Table 1 adds Poisson Loss ZIG, Table 4 introduces CEBRA for behavioral CCA, and Appendices H and J add Gaussian/flow-Gaussian models and behavior-augmented baselines. These methods were not participants in the corresponding v2 comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 introduces configurations for transformer cores, behavioral input channels, and a tuned CEBRA comparison while retaining the principal evaluation metrics and data processing. Its experiment overview changes Table 1's evaluation population from all neurons to half. This establishes a reported setting revision, not a confirmed rerun; other overview entries have inconsistent experiment references.

E4.justification: New analyses test the distribution-versus-mean optimization trade-off, flow-based response modeling, transfer across core architectures, and whether measured behavior can substitute for latents. Existing OOD, stimulus-independence, dimensionality, smoothing, and Monte Carlo analyses are retained. v3 removes v2's report on adapting training masks to small conditioning subsets.

E5.justification: v3 Table 5 adds SEM across three initializations to the feature-vector comparison previously reported without uncertainty in v2 Table 2. Aggregate behavioral CCA uncertainty changes from SEM across mice in v2 Table 12 to variation across cross-validation correlations in v3 Table 4. These disclosures do not establish increased run counts.

E6.justification: Most matched headline scores remain unchanged, but substantial new results cover CEBRA, losses, flows, transformer cores, and behavioral inputs. For example, v3 Table 13 reports conditioned correlations of 0.266 and 0.230 for Poisson- and ZIG-loss latent variants. Reported aggregate CCA values change from 0.57/0.40 to 0.60/0.42, and extrapolation SEM values change from 0.0005/0.0004 to 0.005/0.004.

T1.justification: Appendix H adds a formal flow-based response model, its change-of-variables likelihood, diagonal-Jacobian factorization, and inverse-flow expectation estimator. The original ZIG and variational-inference mathematics remains; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and discussion retain the same central claims: jointly modeling video and latent influences improves response-distribution prediction, neuronal conditioning improves prediction, and learned latents relate to behavior and cortical organization. The introduction consolidates the contribution bullets without materially changing these claims.

C2.justification: v3 strengthens the previously tentative loss trade-off explanation with an experiment, interprets the flow results as supporting ZIG adequacy, and argues that latents capture information beyond measured behavior. It adds qualifications about core quality and tuning, while dropping the small-conditioning-subset mitigation discussion. Residual stimulus information and uncertain biological interpretations of cortical maps were already acknowledged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link, CEBRA search ranges and selected hyperparameters, flow implementation details, and an A100 80GB hardware statement. Appendix B changes the stated inference GPU from H100 to A100. Extensive architecture and hyperparameter documentation was already present in v2; repository accessibility is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The three-category research positioning remains. v3 adds NICE and SENSORIUM 2022 citations, removes Tolhurst et al. and Ustyuzhaninov et al., and expands its treatment of CEBRA. Section 2 also reverses one statement about whether earlier latent models account for sensory input.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: OOD evaluation and stimulus-independence controls move ahead of behavioral and cortical analyses. Numerous paragraphs and headings are rewritten, explanations are expanded, appendices are reorganized, and the impact discussion moves to Appendix O. Acknowledgements and a conference checklist are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column ICML layout to a single-column NeurIPS layout. v2 Figures 3 and 4 are combined into v3 Figure 3, cortical-map panels are rearranged, and numerous figures and tables are relocated or resized. Comparison tables gain columns and new experimental tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: The added controls and CEBRA comparison strengthen validation of the loss trade-off, behavioral relevance, and transfer across cores; implementation disclosures also help reproduction. However, v3 introduces reporting inconsistencies: Appendix H gives a ZIG likelihood of -0.74 while Table 14 reports -0.88, and its ViT superiority wording obscures the distinction between conditioned and unconditioned results. These problems limit the overall gain.
